editorial.marketOverview: The November 19 US cash-market selloff remains the last verified US session: Nasdaq approximately -2.25%, S&P 500 -2.02%, over 90% of S&P constituents lower and VIX 28.44. Reuters November 20 early Asia reporting describes pronounced global risk aversion toward AI equities and falling US Treasury yields amid flight to safety. This regional follow-through reinforces caution but does not supply a synchronized Friday US trading signal.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the 20:58 EST snapshot, Reuters reported Asian equities heading toward their worst week since March 2020, with an approximate 7% weekly decline for its Asia-Pacific index, while yields eased on safety demand. This is geographically and temporally distinct confirmation of risk aversion, not a new US QQQ/SOX market response or material change in the expected three-day path. The 171 curated Open Watch events were unchanged at the last repository refresh.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The existing bearish baseline reflects broad US distribution, volatility expansion and semiconductor underperformance. Asian risk-off adds cross-region corroboration but is not interchangeable with US Friday cash breadth. Treasury easing on safety demand is not necessarily a bullish duration-stock signal when risk premiums rise. Fed expectations remain qualitatively hawkish in Reuters coverage; no direct current FedWatch probability was verified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20 remains a key follow-through test: watch for an attempted rebound and whether QQQ and SOX outperform SPY with breadth improvement. Failure would support weakness Monday November 23 and Tuesday November 24; a sustained semiconductor-led recovery would challenge the bearish outlook. The Friday 10:00 EST Michigan final sentiment and inflation expectations are scheduled events, not realized surprises.
editorial.bullCase: An oversold rebound can follow six consecutive S&P down days. Require synchronized QQQ relative outperformance, SOX/SMH leadership, broad participation, declining VXN/VIX and stable-to-lower yields before reducing downside risk. The Anthropic IPO premium alone does not constitute market-wide recovery.
editorial.bearCase: November 19 Nasdaq -2.25%, broad decliners, VIX 28.44 and semiconductor weakness point to further downside if Friday fails to reclaim leadership. Reuters early Asia losses corroborate global risk aversion, though not US cash-market confirmation. Another failed rebound into Monday would strengthen continuation.
